reason: The compactness inference is false under the stated choice of B: f(B) lying in the target chart does not imply that the coordinate representative F is defined on cl(B), so F(cl(B)) may be meaningless, nor does it imply that F(B) is relatively compact. Concrete counterexample respecting nondegeneracy: take M=R, x=0, f(t)=2t, source chart U=(-2,2) with identity coordinates, target chart V=(-1,1) with coordinate psi(y)=tan(pi*y/2), and B=(-1/2,1/2). Then cl(B) is compact in U, f(B)=V, f fixes 0, and det(I-Df_0)=-1 is nonzero, but F(t)=tan(pi*t) and F(B)=R, so F restricted to B is not compact. The step must instead shrink B so that f(cl(B)) is contained in the target chart (equivalently cl(B) lies in the domain of F); continuity at the fixed point permits this, but the node neither states nor proves it.
